en.title: FAA expands AI air traffic tool SMART to all 22 US en route centers
en.summary: The FAA said it is expanding its AI-assisted traffic planning tool, SMART, to the airspace managed by all 22 US air route traffic control centers. The agency said the tool has helped reroute 180 flights around Washington, saving an average of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per rerouted flight.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it is expanding the use of its AI-assisted traffic planning tool to airspace managed by all 22 US air route traffic control centers. In announcing the expansion on November 10, 2026, the agency said the tool, called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART), had helped reroute 180 flights in the Washington area, with average savings of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per rerouted flight.

SMART draws on 200 data streams, including weather, flight paths, traffic volumes and controller staffing, to help air traffic planners anticipate where demand could exceed capacity and identify opportunities to reroute flights before congestion builds. FAA specialists at the SMART center in Washington review the data and send scheduling recommendations to the agency's Air Traffic Control System Command Center in Warrenton, Virginia, which passes them to the facilities responsible for the affected airspace; local managers then decide whether to act on them.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford unveiled SMART on September 21, 2026, when the agency began limited operations involving flights at Reagan National, Washington Dulles and Baltimore/Washington International airports. The expansion comes even after more than two dozen lawmakers called for a pause in the Washington-area rollout and, in October, asked the FAA to explain how it had tested the system for safety and trained staff to use it; the agency's November 10 update did not address those questions.

zh.title: FAA將AI航管工具SMART擴至全美22個航路管制中心
zh.summary: FAA表示，將把AI輔助航管規劃工具SMART擴大到全美22個航路管制中心管理的空域。該機構表示，這套工具已協助華盛頓地區180架次航班改道，每架次平均節省10分鐘與近80加侖燃油。
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）表示，將把AI輔助航管規劃工具擴大到全美22個航路管制中心管理的空域。該機構在2026年11月10日宣布擴大使用時表示，這套名為「空域、航路與軌跡策略管理」（SMART）的工具已協助華盛頓地區180架次航班改道，每架次平均節省10分鐘與近80加侖燃油。
SMART整合200種資料來源，包括天氣、航路、交通量與管制員人力，協助航管規劃人員預測需求可能超過容量的位置，並在壅塞形成前找出改道機會。FAA位於華盛頓的SMART中心專家審閱資料後，將排程建議送交位於維吉尼亞州沃倫頓的FAA空中交通管制系統指揮中心，再由指揮中心轉交負責相關空域的單位，由當地主管決定是否執行。
運輸部長尚恩·達菲與FAA署長布萊恩·貝德福德於2026年9月21日公布SMART，當時該機構開始在雷根國家機場、華盛頓杜勒斯機場與巴爾的摩／華盛頓國際機場進行有限度運作。儘管已有二十多名國會議員呼籲暫停華盛頓地區的推行，並在10月要求FAA說明如何測試系統安全性與訓練人員使用，FAA仍推動擴大；其11月10日的更新未回應這些問題。
